items.title: Annie Ross — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Another entry in your biography is a trip in 1947 to see your aunt perform on Broadway in Finian’s Rainbow.

ctx.x: Oh, a great vocalist. Never hit a wrong note. I had a friend at school. He played a little bit of piano. He said, “Why don’t we try out.” I said, “Yeah, all right.” So we got together. I always mention him. He didn’t really contribute that much, but he was there. It won. The prize was a recording by Johnny Mercer with Paul Weston and his Orchestra, and the Pied Pipers, of which Jo Stafford was one, and I think about $100. I’m not sure. That’s it there, hanging. That’s the record, Capitol Records. So I can say…

Another entry in your biography is a trip in 1947 to see your aunt perform on Broadway in Finian’s Rainbow. It says, “It awakened an enduring interest in musical theater for you.” But it sounds like you grew up in it. So I’m not sure if that . . .
